one_liner: Microsoft's closed C++ compiler; one Node.js report had it compiling ~2.5x faster than clang-cl, but only versus no-PCH clang-cl.
what_it_does: cl.exe is the C/C++ compiler shipped with Visual Studio and the Build Tools ('Desktop development with C++' workload) and the default MSBuild toolset on Windows. clang-cl is LLVM's driver that accepts cl.exe-style options (/Yc, /Yu, /fp:precise appear in its option table) and installs as an optional Visual Studio component with an MSBuild toolset, so switching between the two is a toolset or CC/CXX change, not a source change. The listed URL is Microsoft's option reference (blocked here); there is no source code and no benchmark behind it.
how_it_is_fast: Nothing measured isolates compiler speed. The reported gap came from precompiled headers: Node's MSVC builds used PCH so shared headers were parsed once, while its gyp setup gave clang-cl no PCH until PR #55249. cl.exe can also compile several sources in parallel inside one invocation (/MP), which clang-cl's option table lists as unsupported, so MSBuild builds that rely on /MP rather than a parallel generator such as Ninja run serially under clang-cl.
when_to_use: Windows-only MSBuild solutions that already depend on cl /MP and /Yc-/Yu precompiled headers, where moving to clang-cl without Ninja-style parallelism and PCH would lengthen builds
C++/CLI code (/clr), which clang-cl's option table lists as unsupported
Debug-build edit-compile loops on Windows, where Lemire's 2023 'Visual Studio versus ClangCL' post (search snippet only) says MSVC compiles faster than ClangCL
when_not_to_use: Throughput-bound SIMD or parsing code: simdjson parsed twitter.json at 1.31 GB/s built with MSVC 19.25 vs 2.22 GB/s with ClangCL 9.0 (ClangCL 1.70x, derived from page data), and llama.cpp PR #10668 measured clang with Ninja 15.68% faster prompt processing than MSVC on an AMD 7600X
Projects that track Node.js or V8: Node.js 24.0.0 (2025-05-06) removed MSVC support and requires ClangCL on Windows
CPU-heavy Windows on ARM builds: llama.cpp's build docs say MSVC's ARM NEON intrinsic support may be incomplete, and its release workflow builds the CPU backend with clang
Cross-platform or open toolchains: cl.exe is closed-source and runs only on Windows hosts
As evidence of a compile-time edge: no equal-settings (both with PCH, both parallel) comparison was found; the only ratio compares PCH with no PCH

integration.form: compiler toolchain (closed-source binary in Visual Studio / Build Tools)
integration.dependencies: Visual Studio or Build Tools with the 'Desktop development with C++' workload (MSVC STL, Windows SDK)
integration.min_toolchain: not applicable; the cited issue names no MSVC version, and Node's current build guide targets Visual Studio 2026 or VS 2022 17.14
integration.platforms: Windows hosts; x64 and ARM64 targets (Node lists ARM64/ARM64EC build tools)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — both take cl.exe-style options and plug into MSBuild as platform toolsets, but code that now requires Clang (Node.js 24+ with its V8) will not build with cl.exe, and in the other direction clang-cl ignores /MP and rejects /clr

gotchas: The ~2.5x figure (no hardware, versions, flags or timings; 'less with x64, more with ARM64') compares MSVC with precompiled headers against clang-cl without them; Node PR #55249 enabled PCH for clang-cl through gyp-next (merged 2024-10-11, backported to v22.12.0) and published no before/after numbers, so the evidence measures a build-configuration difference that no longer exists.

clang-cl lists /MP under unsupported options, so reports that clang-cl builds are several times slower in MSBuild projects (a llama.cpp-related search snippet cites 3-4x) usually measure lost per-invocation parallelism; build with Ninja or another parallel generator before comparing.

Clang does not instantiate templates into a PCH by default (-fpch-instantiate-templates defaults off), but clang-cl /Yc turns it on by default in current LLVM's driver; a January 2020 cfe-dev thread (search snippet only) reported clang-cl PCH builds about 3x slower than MSVC for one codebase before that change, so older comparisons may not hold.

Lemire's Node issue #52809 (May 2024) calls a warm-ccache ClangCL build of 15-20 minutes an improvement over MSVC but gives no MSVC figure; cached versus uncached, so it is not an equal-settings counter-measurement either.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The catalogued siblings (icpx, AOCC, zapcc, TinyCC, MIR/c2m, cg_clif) target generated-code speed or one-shot compile speed, mostly on Linux; pick MSVC only for Windows MSBuild solutions that need cl.exe-specific features such as /clr or /MP-driven builds, and prefer clang-cl or icpx (intel/llvm also builds on 64-bit Windows) when runtime speed matters.
verified_claims_summary: A Node.js Windows build contributor reported in October 2024 that building Node with vcbuild.bat clang-cl took about 2.5x as long as with MSVC, with no hardware, versions, flags or timings, and attributed the gap to clang-cl builds lacking precompiled headers; the PCH fix for clang-cl landed eleven days later without numbers. No measurement of cl.exe versus clang-cl at equal build settings was found.
status_note: Actively shipped with Visual Studio but closed-source and Windows-only, so usability is reference; the evidence workload is gone, since Node.js 24 (May 2025) dropped MSVC builds and requires ClangCL.
